title: Auric Telecom — inference ops digest (call + constraints)
content:
Call summary (2025-11-04)
- Participants: Auric (Infra: Samir K., Platform: Lian Zhao), Customer success (Rita), Redwood: Maya (SE), Diego (Solutions), Priya (SRE).
- Goal: quick intake - what does Auric need for production LLM assistant on operator consoles (ticket routing, log summarization, intent extraction).

Key customer constraints (raw capture)
- Network: Strict egress policy, only outbound to specific IP ranges, must flow through corporate egress proxy (TLS inspection) — no general internet access for inference nodes.
- Data residency: initial rollout must live in AWS eu-west-1 for regulatory reasons.
- KMS/HSM: keys must be stored in Auric KMS, HSM-backed signing for audit events.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms for single-turn 32-64 token responses for operator UI interactions.
- Throughput: expected steady 120 reqs/min for phase 1 (peak bursts up to 800 reqs/min during incident windows).
- Model fidelity: good summarization of semi-structured logs (4–6 short bullets), must preserve redaction markers; hallucination tolerance low — false positives problematic.
- Compliance: full request/response audit logs retained for 90 days (redactions applied on vector store output).

Technical gotchas noted on call
- Egress proxy blocks default Redwood agent telemetry; need explicit allowlist for control-plane callbacks.
- Auric's VLAN segmentation prevents GPUs from being placed in same subnet as management plane; will require private peering or a jump proxy.
- Long context windows are not needed; prompts are small but retrieval will add 2–3 short docs -> KV cache helpful but must be bounded due to memory limits on smaller gpus.
- On-prem hardware inventory is older (A100-40GB and some T4s). Quantization profiles recommended for A100-40GB; T4s need a different runtime path and may increase latency.

Model & deployment options (initial thoughts)
- Candidate models: rw-7b-quant-v2 (fast, low cost) vs rw-13b-qt (higher fidelity, higher latency). Recommend start with rw-7b-quant + retrieval re-rank fallback to rw-13b for flagged queries.
- Deployment: Redwood Private in eu-west-1 VPC (customer-managed networking) to satisfy residency + KMS integration. Dedicated pools for production (SLA) and a small dev pool for testing.
- Autoscaling: configure burst capacity policy to allow extra capacity during incident windows, with pre-warmed instances to meet p95 goal.

Initial sizing & rough cost/latency sketch (very rough)
- Expected per-request token usage: prompt 120 tokens, response 40 tokens (short summaries).
- RW-7B-quant on A100-40GB: median small prompt completion ~80–120ms; p95 depends on batching, estimate ~180–220ms.
- Throughput on 1 A100-40GB (rw-7b): ~200–350 rps (small tokens) if continuously batched; given real-world variance and TTL constraints, plan on 60–80 rps per GPU for consistent p95.
- For peak 800 reqs/min (~13 rps), a single GPU pool of 2–3 A100s with autoscale buffer should suffice; but because of egress and network jitter, recommend Dedicated pool with autoscale to 5 GPUs for headroom during incidents.

Observability & audit requirements
- Logs: token-level cost is not acceptable to send raw tokens; implement structured event logs: prompt-id, embedding-hash (for retrieval), response-hash, redaction flag, latency, model-version. Keep raw payloads in customer-managed S3 with lifecycle rules.
- Tracing: attach request-id to all logs and span through retrieval, model call, and post-processing for easy triage in Console.
- Alerts: regression alert on generation quality (eval set of 30 prompts daily). Hook Redwood Optimize quality monitor to send alerts when hallucination rates exceed 2%.

Fallbacks and graceful degradation
- If the primary model can't meet p95 → automatic fallback to lower-latency rw-7b-quant with a shorter prompt template (less retrieval) and add a confidence meta-flag back to UI.
- If Private pool capacity exhausted, route to a 'restricted-hosted' variant in eu-west-1 with stricter data handling (audit in place). Need legal sign-off.

Open questions (to resolve before proposal)
- Legal: is routing to restricted-hosted acceptable under their contract during outages? (Flagged for CS/legal).
- KMS: can we register Auric's HSM for signing webhooks/callbacks or do we need to proxy via our control plane?
- Network: confirm exact egress proxy allowlist IPs and whether agent can originate from an allowed jump-host.
- Retention: 90-day audit retention — will Auric accept aggregated logs (hashes + pointers) or need full plaintext stored?

Action items (owners + suggested dates)
- Diego: build a minimal dev blueprint for Private in eu-west-1 showing VPC peering patterns and egress proxy workarounds. Due: 2025-11-10.
- Priya: run latency microbenchmarks for rw-7b-quant & rw-13b on A100-40GB and T4 (use sample prompts from Auric). Due: 2025-11-12.
- Maya: draft proposal (arch + cost delta + fallback policy) and circulate to Auric + Solutions leadership. Due: 2025-11-14.
- Rita (Auric): confirm KMS/HSM constraints and provide contact in infra team for network allowlist. Due: 2025-11-07.

Notes to self / quick heuristics
- Keep retrieval small: 2 docs + high-precision rerank; excessive retrieval increases hallucination risk.
- Use prefix caching aggressively for operator-facing prompts to shave off 30–50ms where possible.
- When proposing Dedicated pool sizing, show two scenarios: normal ops (2 GPUs) and incident ops (scale to 5) with explicit cost delta numbers.

Meeting follow-up plan
- Share this digest with Auric and request answers to Open questions + allowlist info.
- Schedule technical deep-dive (30–45m) with Auric infra and Redwood SRE to validate peering/egress approach.
- After Priya's perf numbers, update proposal and include cost sensitivity table (p50/p95 latency vs GPUs vs model).

Random fragments captured (raw)
- "If ops want 80ms p50 we'd need pre-warmed pool + tiny prompt templates."
- "redact:{user_ssn} must be preserved - do not send to hosted log"
- Possible legal anchor: add a clause for emergency cross-region fallbacks with customer consent.

End of digest.
summary: Informal intake notes and ops constraints from Auric Telecom call: residency, KMS, latency SLOs, network egress, model/deployment options, gotchas, action items.
